name: modified Bullard disk dynamo
question: Does the disk dynamo become a switch between the two polarities of its field when another parameter is the control?

carrier.name: magnetic flux components x and y and disk angular velocity Z

closure: The variables are coupled through the three explicit dynamo equations; x and y are the magnetic-flux components, Z is the disk angular velocity, and the externally applied torque is represented by the g-dependent term.
observable: The paper analyzes the magnetic-flux components and the disk angular velocity, including the onset of dynamo instability around the zero-flux state x = y = 0 with Z = Z0.
assumptions: The modified Bullard disk-dynamo model neglects additional magnetic-feedback effects beyond the terms explicitly present in the three source equations.
The parameters q, m, g, and f are treated as constants.
The linear stability discussion uses the equilibrium Z = Z0 and x = y = 0.

provenance.source: N. Leprovost, B. Dubrulle and F. Plunian, Intermittency in the homopolar disk-dynamo, Magnetohydrodynamics 42, 131 (2006), arXiv:nlin/0506050
provenance.kind: equations of the source paper, as extracted from its LaTeX
